advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test showing `fsck_cli(["--repair", "--only", "stale-channel"], ...)` gets past `--only` validation and behaves the same as `--only=stale-channel` (e.g. extend test_stale_only_cli_skips_unrelated_ensure_sweep to run both spellings).
evidence: tests/unit/test_fsck_only_flag.py parametrizes `fsck_cli(["--only", value])` without `--repair`, so the stale-channel case always stops at "--only=stale-channel requires --repair" (src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py:368-370).
The only success-path test uses the equals form: tests/interfaces/store/test_fsck_stale_channel_repair.py:200 `rc = fsck.fsck_cli(["--repair", "--only=stale-channel"], repo_root=str(tmp_path))`.
The commit message says the bug was that 'an operator following the help could not scope anything'. That scoped path (`--repair --only stale-channel`) has no test.
advisory.finding: No test runs the newly allowed space spelling on the path that should succeed. Every case in test_fsck_only_flag.py returns 2 at validation. `["--repair", "--only", "stale-channel"]` is never shown to get past the `--only` checks and reach repair the way `--only=stale-channel` does.
scenarios: A later change to the strip filter at fsck.py:380-386 or to `_fsck_govern` that mishandles the folded token would break `--repair --only stale-channel` while every test stays green.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a case `fsck_cli(["--only", "--repair"])` asserting rc == 2 and '--only requires a value' in stderr.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py:328-329: "A bare trailing ``--only`` (or one followed by another flag) stays bare and is still reported as missing its value."
src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py:335: `if arg == "--only" and i + 1 < len(argv) and not argv[i + 1].startswith("-"):`
tests/unit/test_fsck_only_flag.py only tests `fsck_cli(["--repair", "--only"])` (trailing); there is no case like `["--only", "--repair"]`.
advisory.finding: The new `_join_only_value` docstring promises that a bare `--only` followed by another flag stays bare. Only the trailing-`--only` case is tested. `["--only", "--repair"]` (bare `--only` in the middle of argv, next token a flag) is never exercised.
scenarios: If the `startswith("-")` guard is dropped, `["--only", "--repair"]` becomes `--only=--repair`. It then fails as an unknown value instead of 'requires a value', and `--repair` is silently consumed. No test would catch this.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Have the help test check the `--only` line of `build_fsck(prog=...).format_help()` rather than `parser._actions`.
evidence: tests/unit/test_fsck_only_flag.py: `action = next(a for a in parser._actions if "--only" in a.option_strings)` / `return f"{action.help} {action.choices}"`
src/rebar/_cli/_store_commands.py:61: `text = factory(prog=f"rebar store {name}").format_help()` is what users actually see.
advisory.finding: The help test reads argparse's private `parser._actions` and builds its own string from `action.help` and `action.choices`. It does not check what `rebar store fsck --help` actually prints, which is rendered by `factory(...).format_help()`. That ties the test to argparse internals rather than to the visible help.
scenarios: If `--only` is declared in a way that changes the rendered help without changing `action.help`, or argparse internals change, this test would not track the text users see.

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Fold `--limit <N>` into `--limit=<N>` the same way as `--only`, or reject a bare `--limit` with 'requires a value', so a space-separated limit is never silently ignored.
evidence: src/rebar/_cli/_parsers/core/repair.py:54: parser.add_argument("--limit", metavar="N", help="check at most N tickets")

src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py:373-374: for a in argv:
        if a.startswith("--limit="):
src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py:388: fmt, _rest = parse_output(argv, "report")  (the leftover args, including '--limit' and '5', are discarded)
src/rebar/_engine_support/output.py:122-125: unrecognised args are appended to `rest` and never rejected
blocking.finding: The `--limit` flag has the same help/parse mismatch this change fixes for `--only`, but the fix was not applied to it. The parser renders it as `--limit N`, which implies a space-separated value. `fsck_cli` only recognises `--limit=`. With `--limit 5`, neither token is removed, both fall through to `parse_output`, and its leftover args (`_rest`) are thrown away. The limit is silently ignored and fsck/repair runs over every ticket.
scenarios: An operator follows `rebar store fsck --help` and runs `rebar store fsck --repair --limit 5`. The repair runs over the whole store instead of 5 tickets, and no error is shown.
blocking.suggested_fix: Generalise `_join_only_value` to cover both `--only` and `--limit` (e.g. `_join_flag_values(argv, ("--only", "--limit"))`). Also treat a leftover bare `--limit` as an error ('--limit requires a value'), matching how `--only` is handled.
